lem-nrqm-central-exponential-moments:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real
$\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda
r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and

$$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$

The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel
function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are
asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about
complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.
lem-nrqm-central-positive-scaling-spectr:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator with spectral projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel
$\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $c>0$. Write $cA$ for the operator
with $D(cA):=D(A)$ and $(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$, and for $m_{c}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
$m_{c}(\lambda):=c\lambda$, define
$$F(B):=E\bigl(m_{c}^{-1}(B)\bigr)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
Then:

(a) $F$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$;

(b) for every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the bounded integrals
satisfy $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f\circ m_{c})$, and the operator
$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)$ of the spectral theorem equals $cA$ with
domain $D(A)$;

(c) consequently $F$ is the spectral projection valued measure $E_{cA}$ of
$cA$: for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{cA}(B)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr);$$in particular the negative spectral subspaces agree,$$E_{cA}\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H=E\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H .$$

The assertion transfers the spectral measure along positive scaling of the
operator. It asserts no spectral type of a particular operator, no multiplicity
statement and no physical interpretation; $c<0$ is not covered, and no
statement is made about unbounded Borel functions of $cA$ beyond the identity
functional calculus stated in (b).
lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-different:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let $H_{0}$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=3$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem.
Let $D^{2}_{j}$ denote the second weak partial derivative in the $j$-th
coordinate, defined componentwise on the locally integrable classes of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]),
write $\Delta_{w}:=D^{2}_{1}+D^{2}_{2}+D^{2}_{3}$ for the weak Laplacian
(defined on the classes whose three second weak partial derivatives lie in
$L^{2}$), and let $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_{0}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\Delta_{w}f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_{0});$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_{2}(H_{0}f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^{2}$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, the
operator $H_{0}+M_{V}$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain
$D(H_{0})$, coincides with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf$
on the same domain; in particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ the eigenvalue equation
$(H_{0}+M_{V})\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

def-nrqm-central-framework-central-poten.physical_scope: The pair's declared central-potential model for one spinless massive particle: its state space, its position and momentum assignments, its assigned energy operator for a real bounded measurable central potential, its declared spherical angular-radial reading and effective potential, and its stationary-state, bound-state and continuum-threshold vocabulary. The model is an additional assumption of the pair, not a derivation from the three-dimensional massive-particle model P5; the Coulomb and other unbounded or singular potentials, spin, relativistic and radiative corrections, finite nuclear size and external fields are excluded and are introduced only by their own later items. No identification of a concrete material system with the model, no empirical value and no measured energy are asserted.

def-nrqm-central-framework-central-poten:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared central-potential model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **central-potential model**. Its declared
state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of clause (a), with the
position and momentum families $Q_{j}$, $P_{k}$ of that clause
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). A **declared central
potential** of the model is a function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ of the
form $V(x):=v(|x|)$ for $x\ne0$, where $v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is real,
bounded and measurable and $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\|v\|_{\infty}=\sup_{r>0}|v(r)|$ is
finite; the assignment $V(0):=0$ is a declared convention that does not affect
the $L^{2}$ theory. The potential energy is read in joules. The model declares
the **Born position law** of the framework for a unit class $\psi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}),$$
the spin-zero reading of clause (b) of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]. The pair asserts no derivation
of a central force law from $H_{0}$ or from P5: the restriction to a declared
central potential is an assumption of the model, and an assignment of a
concrete material system to the model is an identification in the sense of
clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$. With $M_{V}$ the
bounded multiplication operator of clause (a) of the same theorem, the
**assigned energy operator** of the model with central potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. By clause (c) of the cited theorem
$H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{V})$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$\Delta_{w}=D_{1}^{2}+D_{2}^{2}+D_{3}^{2}$ the weak Laplacian of that lemma, so
that on any open set on which $V$ is of class $C^{2}$ the model's
time-independent equation is the ordinary differential equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ for a $C^{2}$ representative. The
model adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its declared energy observable; its
self-adjointness is the cited theorem's, and no further spectral property is
presupposed here.

**(d) The declared spherical reading.** Let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from
$H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$, written
$U\psi=(u_{lm})_{l\ge0,-l\le m\le l}$, and let $(Y_{lm})$ be the complete
orthonormal family of that theorem. As an additional reading of the model, the
pair declares the **spherical sector** $(l,m)$ and the **effective potential**
$$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r):=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\qquad(r>0),$$
whose second summand is called the **angular-momentum barrier**; both
summands, and $v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}$, are read in joules. The model's
**declared radial equation** in the sector $(l,m)$ is the eigenvalue equation
for the one-dimensional expression
$$u\longmapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u,\qquad u:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C,$$
restricted to declared admissible classes (for instance $u\in
C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$). The pair does not presuppose that the assigned
energy operator of clause (c) literally reduces to this expression; the
consistency of the two readings on smooth states is the content of the
spherical-reduction theorem of this page, which is proved from the cited
mathematics. The angular-momentum quantum numbers $l$ and $m$
appearing in the reading are labels of the orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$; the
identification of $l$ with a total angular momentum of a material system is a
separate assignment of the framework's angular-momentum items and is not made
here.

**(e) Stationary and bound-state vocabulary.** A **stationary vector** of the
model with potential $V$ and **energy** $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
vector with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalised, $\|\psi\|=1$; its
eigenvalue is its **binding energy**, read in joules, and the value $0$ is
called the **continuum threshold** of the model. The model reads the energy
outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$
as the point mass $\delta_{E}$, the reading of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
position density of that preparation as $|\psi|^{2}$ by clause (b). These are
declarations of the model under P2; they construct no sample, detector or
measured value, and they assert no stability, decay or formation claim.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
state space, position and momentum assignments, an assigned energy operator
for a real bounded measurable central potential, a declared spherical reading
with its effective potential and radial equation, and a stationary-state and
bound-state vocabulary. They introduce no assumption beyond P1, P2, P4, P5,
P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; in particular the central form of the
potential, the model's use of the full three-dimensional space as its state
space and the identification of the spherical sectors with angular-momentum
labels are declarations of the pair. The model excludes from its scope, until
their own items introduce them: the Coulomb potential $\propto-1/r$ and other
unbounded or singular potentials; spin and magnetic couplings; relativistic
corrections; finite nuclear size; the radiation extension, spontaneous
emission and radiation reaction; external electromagnetic fields; and any
many-body or shielding modification of a central potential. No numerical value
of $m$, $\hbar$ or of any potential is fixed here, and no empirical result is
asserted.

pthm-nrqm-central-spherical-reduction-of.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared central-potential model of this pair: a smooth reduced function u compactly supported away from the origin, transported to the three-dimensional vector psi = u(r)Y_lm(Omega)/r of the spherical sector (l,m), lies in the model's energy domain, and the model's assigned energy acts on psi by the declared radial differential expression with the effective potential v(r) + hbar^2 l(l+1)/(2 m r^2); consequently the radial equation holds almost everywhere exactly when the linear operator equation holds on that vector, including the zero vector. A nonzero reduced function alone defines a pure preparation, whose position law is normalized and which is stationary when the radial equation holds. The statement is an exact identity for the declared model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no converse for arbitrary reduced classes, no completeness of any family of radial solutions, no spectral classification, no measured energy and no empirical result, and it excludes the Coulomb potential from its hypotheses, which are treated by the following items of the page.

pthm-nrqm-central-spherical-reduction-of:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared
central-potential model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=0$, a real bounded measurable central potential
$V(x)=v(|x|)$ and assigned energy operator $H_{V}$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $l\ge0$, $-l\le \bar m\le l$, let
$u\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, and define
$$\psi(x):=\frac{u(r)}{r}Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega,\ r=|x|>0),$$
with $(Y_{lm})$ the complete orthonormal family and $U$ the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]]. Then:

(a) $\psi$ lies in $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\})\subseteq
H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=D(H_{V})$, its image under $U$ is the
finite-support vector whose only potentially nonzero entry is the $(l,\bar m)$-entry $u$,
and $B\mapsto\int_B|\psi|^2dx$ is its position quadratic measure. For $u\not\equiv0$, the unit vector $\widehat\psi:=\psi/\|\psi\|$ represents its pure preparation and has position outcome law
$$\mu^G_{\widehat\psi}(B)=\|\psi\|^{-2}\int_B|\psi|^2dx;$$

(b) for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$,
$$H_{V}\psi(x)=\frac{1}{r}\Bigl[-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u(r)\Bigr]Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega),$$
the two sides being equal as $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ classes; thus
the model's assigned energy acts on the smooth spherical sector by the
declared radial differential expression with effective potential
$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r)=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}$;

(c) if $E\in\mathbb R$ and $u$ satisfies the declared radial equation
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u(r)=Eu(r)\qquad(0<r<\infty)$$
pointwise on $(0,\infty)$, then $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$, when $u\not\equiv0$, $\psi$ is a nonzero stationary vector of the model with energy $E$ and the pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, every assigned sharp observable having a time-independent outcome law in it. For $u=0$, only the linear identity $H_V0=E0$ is asserted and no pure preparation is assigned;

(d) for every $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, including $u=0$,
the radial equation
$$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}u^{\prime\prime}(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^2l(l+1)}{2mr^2}\Bigr)u(r)=Eu(r)$$
holds for almost every $r>0$ if and only if $H_V\psi=E\psi$ as Hilbert-space vectors. If $v$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$, this radial equality is also equivalent to its pointwise version. For general measurable $v$, no pointwise converse is asserted.

The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared model; it
asserts no converse for general reduced functions, no completeness of any
family of radial solutions, no discrete spectrum, and no measured energy, and
it does not apply to the Coulomb potential, whose self-adjointness and spectral
theory are supplied separately.

def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-h.physical_scope: The pair's declared Coulomb model, in a one-centre form for a spinless particle of declared mass and coupling in a fixed centre, and in a two-body form for two distinguishable spinless massive particles of opposite charge with the Coulomb pair potential -kappa/|x1-x2|; the declared centre-of-mass/relative decomposition with reduced mass mu, the declared identification of the hydrogen-like atom with the model for declared charge and mass parameters, and the model's scope exclusions. The item fixes model assumptions and readings of P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and P7 together with cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical identification, no measured constant, no transition, photon or line-intensity claim, and no spectral or scattering consequence, which are supplied by the theorems of the page or by later radiation and scattering items. Spin, relativistic and QED corrections, finite nuclear size, external fields, many-body and shielding effects and radiation reaction are excluded.

def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-h:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data of clause (a) of the declared
central-potential model [[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]
with a declared mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, the state space
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the componentwise position and momentum
families and the action constant $\hbar>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared one-centre Coulomb model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix a real **coupling** $\kappa>0$ with the declared
unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and put
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{m^{-1}}),\qquad C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\ \text{ on }\ D(C_{\gamma})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
the self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] clause (c). The **assigned
energy operator** of the one-centre Coulomb model is
$$H_{\kappa}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,C_{\gamma},$$
with domain $D(H_{\kappa}):=D(C_{\gamma})$; by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a)
and (b) it is self-adjoint with the same domain, and by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] together with
the action formula of the cited theorem it acts by
$$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa\frac{f}{|\cdot|}\qquad(f\in D(H_{\kappa})),$$
where $\Delta_{w}$ is the weak Laplacian. The model declares the **length
scale** $a_{\kappa}:=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, read in metres, and the **energy
scale** $\mathcal E_{\kappa}:=m\kappa^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})=\hbar^{2}/(2ma_{\kappa}^{2})$,
read in joules. The model adopts $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ as its declared
energy observable for the one-centre problem; the self-adjointness is the
cited theorem's and no spectral property is presupposed here.

**(c) The declared radial reading of the one-centre model.** Let $U$ and
$(A_{l})_{l\ge0}$ be the unitary and the radial operators of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] clauses (a)-(d):
$U$ maps $H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$ with
$UH_{\kappa}U^{*}=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$, and each $A_{l}$ is self-adjoint
with form domain $V_{l}$ and domain $D(A_{l})$. The model declares the
**sector $(l,m)$ radial energy operator** $A_{l}^{(\kappa)}:=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$,
read in joules, and, for a class $u\in D(A_{l})$, the **declared radial
equation** is the distributional identity
$$-u''(r)+\Bigl(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}-\frac{\gamma}{r}\Bigr)u(r)=A_{l}u(r)\qquad\text{on }(0,\infty),$$
which by clause (c) of the cited theorem is an ordinary differential equation
with $C^{2}$ representative whenever $A_{l}u=Eu$ for a constant $E$. The
**regular reduced solution** at energy attribute $k>0$ is the function
$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$ of clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]], with $v$ the regular
power series of that clause; the pair uses it as the declared radial template
of the model, not as a physical state, until the normalisation and spectral
theorems of the page identify it.

**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries $-q$ and particle 2 carries $+q$, with a real **charge parameter**
$q>0$ (unit C). Declare the **pair coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q^{2}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$
is a constitutive assumption of the model, and $\kappa$ is read in
$\mathrm{J\,m}$. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

**(e) The hydrogen-like identification.** A **hydrogen-like ion** assignment of
the two-body model is the choice $m_{1}=m_{\mathrm e}$ (electron mass
parameter), $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm n}$ (nuclear mass parameter) and $q=e$ (the
elementary charge of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) with nuclear charge $+Ze$, so that
$\kappa=Ze^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ for a declared positive integer $Z$;
$Z=1$ with a proton mass parameter $m_{\mathrm p}$ is the **hydrogen
assignment**. These assignments use empirical mass and charge parameters; any
comparison of the model's consequences with a laboratory hydrogen atom is a
tested identification in the sense of clause (iii) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and carries the
uncertainty of that identification. The model declares no numerical value of
$m_{\mathrm e},m_{\mathrm n},e,\mu_{0}$ or $\hbar$; numerical evaluations, when
made, use their declared or measured values as explicitly qualified empirical
inputs.

**(f) Scope exclusions.** Until their own items introduce them, the Coulomb
and hydrogen models exclude: spin, magnetic moment couplings and
spin–statistics assignments beyond the trivial spin-zero factor; relativistic
corrections, in particular any fine-structure splitting of the degeneracy of
the gross-structure levels; finite nuclear size, nuclear recoil beyond the
two-body reduction of clause (d), and nuclear structure; QED corrections such
as vacuum polarisation and the Lamb shift, and hyperfine structure; shielding
and many-body modification of the $1/r$ potential; the radiation extension,
spontaneous emission, radiation reaction and any photon, transition-frequency
or line-intensity statement; external electromagnetic fields; and any
scattering, ionisation or continuum process, which belongs to the scattering
items of the quantum-mechanics track. The model asserts no empirical result
and fixes no measured quantity.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observa.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared one-centre Coulomb model and the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5: the model's assigned energy is a sharp observable on H^2 with essential spectrum [0,infinity) and negative spectrum consisting only of isolated finite-multiplicity discrete eigenvalues; its flow is the strongly continuous unitary group of P4 with the norm-differentiable Schroedinger equation exactly on the domain; its stationary preparations are exactly the eigenrays with point-mass energy law; and position and energy readings coexist. The item asserts no measured energy, no apparatus, no eigenvalue list or degeneracy, no transition or radiation statement and no empirical result; it does not identify the coupling, mass or charge with any measured constants.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observa:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared one-centre
Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ on $D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
assigned sharp-observable reading
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the flow and
preparation reading [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and
the spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model:
$H_{\kappa}$ is densely defined, self-adjoint and bounded below on
$D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, acts by
$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa f/|\cdot|$, and
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=[0,+\infty);$$
every point of $\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ is an eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity, isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of negative eigenvalues is
at most countable;

(b) *Flow.* The family $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is the model's
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{0}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure preparation
$[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and only if
$\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$; in that case, with eigenvalue $E$,
one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ for a normalised $\psi$, and every bounded assigned sharp
observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in
this preparation;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

(e) *Spectral support and exact values.* For every preparation $\rho$ one has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$, and an exact energy value
$\lambda$ has $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue, in which case the probability is the total weight of the
eigenspace; in particular no exact value in $\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(H_{\kappa})$
is admissible, and the item asserts neither that $0$ is an eigenvalue nor any
statement about eigenvalues in the positive half-line, which are excluded by
the following radial items;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no eigenvalue list, no
degeneracy, no transition, radiation or line-intensity statement, no
identification of $\kappa$, $m$ or $\hbar$ with measured constants, and no
empirical result.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared one-centre Coulomb model with parameters hbar, m, kappa: the model's bound energies are exactly E_n = -m kappa^2/(2 hbar^2 n^2), the level n carrying an n^2-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the transported Laguerre solutions, the bound states forming a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace, and the nonnegative spectral subspace containing no eigenvectors and being infinite dimensional, so the bound states alone do not exhaust the model's state space. The item asserts no measured spectral line, no transition rate, no photon, no light-matter coupling and no empirical result, and it does not assert absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace of the scaled model, which is recorded for the unscaled operator by the cited mathematics.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum:
## Statement

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ with length scale $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and
the energy-observable content of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le m\le l$ let
$\psi_{nlm}$ be the regular bound solutions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] and put
$\Psi_{nlm}:=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$, and put
$$E_{n}:=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}\qquad(n\ge1).$$
Then:

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nlm}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\Psi_{nlm}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(b) the eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $E_{n}$, $n\ge1$;
the eigenspace of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ is exactly
$\operatorname{span}\{\Psi_{nlm}:0\le l\le n-1,\ -l\le m\le l\}$, so the model
assigns to the level $n$ the **model degeneracy** $n^{2}$; in particular
$H_{\kappa}$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,+\infty)$, whose spectral content is
entirely essential spectrum $[0,+\infty)$ in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] (a);

(c) the family
$(\Psi_{nlm})_{n\ge1,\,0\le l\le n-1,\,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal
family of the negative spectral subspace
$E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the bound states
span exactly the preparations whose energy outcomes are negative almost surely;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The values $E_{n}$ are model
parameters determined by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; no numerical value, no measured
line, no transition rate, no photon or light-matter coupling and no empirical
result is asserted. The absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace
is recorded by the cited mathematics for the unscaled operator and is not
restated for the scaled model here.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-ra.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared one-centre Coulomb model: the position outcome law of any normalised bound state, its disintegration into the radial density |u_nl|^2/||u_nl||^2 times the angular spherical-harmonic weight, and the explicit ground-state density, its mean radius 3 a_kappa/2, its mode a_kappa, the positivity of the probability in every ball around the origin and the absence of an atomic probability at the origin. The scales a_kappa and the density are model data; the item asserts no measured radius, no orbit, no trajectory, no formation or decay process, and does not identify a_kappa with any measured length.

pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-ra:
## Statement

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2 and P5, the readings of the declared
one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, $\kappa>0$ and length scale
$a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, the energy-observable reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]], the bound-state data
of [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], and the
spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For each label let $\psi_{nlm}$ and
$\Psi_{nlm}=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$ be the bound vectors of the cited
theorem, and write $u_{nl}$ for the reduced regular solution with
$\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$. Then:

(a) for every label and every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ the position
outcome law in the unit preparation $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{-2}\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)\,|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr;$$
in particular, for a **radial** set $B=\{x:a<|x|<b\}$ with
$0\le a<b\le+\infty$ one has
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\frac{1}{\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\,dr,$$
so the **radial density** $p_{nl}(r):=|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$ is a
probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p_{nl}\ge0$ and
$\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}(r)\,dr=1$;

(b) for $n=1,l=m=0$ one has
$$\Psi_{100}(x)=(\pi a_{\kappa}^{3})^{-1/2}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}},\qquad p_{10}(r)=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}},$$
the mean of $p_{10}$ is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{10}(r)\,dr=3a_{\kappa}/2$, the
unique maximum of $p_{10}$ is at $r=a_{\kappa}$, the spatial density
$|\Psi_{100}|^{2}$ is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin,
and for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{100}}\bigl(\{|x|<\varepsilon\}\bigr)=\frac{1}{6}\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^{3}+O(\varepsilon^{4})>0,$$
which tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$: the density maximum at the
origin is not an atom of probability at any point;

(c) for every label the reduced solution has the polynomial-exponential form
$$u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}\,r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na_{\kappa})}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}\bigl(2r/(na_{\kappa})\bigr)\qquad(c_{nl}\ne0),$$
with $L_{j}^{(a)}$ the Laguerre polynomial of integer order, so the radial
density of the level $(n,l)$ is a polynomial times $r^{2l+2}$ times a
decreasing exponential, and its normalisation constant is fixed by
$\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}|^{2}dr=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{2}$;

(d) *Reading and scope.* The statements are conditional on P1, P2, P5, the
declared Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The radial density is the
reading of the model's position observable on radial sets; it is not a
trajectory, an orbit or a definite distance, and the model assigns positive
probability to every open ball around the origin and to arbitrarily large
radii. No measured radius, no measured density and no identification of
$a_{\kappa}$ with a laboratory length is asserted; numerical comparison
requires the measured constants as qualified empirical inputs and is deferred.

pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-thres.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared two-body Coulomb model with masses m1, m2, charge parameter q and coupling kappa: the centre-of-mass/relative decomposition U_Phi H_2 U_Phi^(-1) = T_R (x) I + I (x) C_mu, the identification of the relative problem with the one-centre Coulomb model of mass mu, the relative gross-structure levels E_n^mu = -mu kappa^2/(2 hbar^2 n^2) with degeneracy n^2 within the relative problem, the fact that the total two-body Hamiltonian has no eigenvalues and continuous negative spectrum with the relative levels as thresholds, and the absence of normalisable states of definite total momentum. The item asserts no measured level, no transition, no photon, no external-field or many-body effect and no empirical result; it does not model binding or formation dynamics and does not identify the parameters with measured masses or charges.

pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-thres:
## Statement

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared two-body Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a), (b),
(d) and (e) with declared masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, charge parameter $q>0$,
coupling $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$, reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map
$\Phi$, its unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the total operator $H_{2}$ on
$H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$, the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}$
and the relative operator $C_{\mu}$, together with the one-centre results
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] applied with mass
parameter $\mu$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the identity $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$
holds on the tensor product, and $C_{\mu}$ is exactly the one-centre Coulomb
operator of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
parameter $\mu$; the model's relative problem is therefore the declared
one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$;

(b) the relative bound energies are
$$\mathcal E_{n}:=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu a_{\mu}^{2}n^{2}},\qquad a_{\mu}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{\mu\kappa}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
with model degeneracy $n^{2}$ within the relative problem and the same radial
and position readings as in
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] with $m$
replaced by $\mu$;

(c) the total operator $H_{2}$ has no eigenvalues at all:
$\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},+\infty)$, the whole negative
part $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},0)$ of the spectrum is continuous,
and each relative bound energy $\mathcal E_{n}$ is a threshold of the
continuous spectrum of $H_{2}$ rather than an eigenvalue;

(d) if $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $u$ is a relative
bound vector with $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$, then the product vector
$\varphi\otimes u$ is an eigenvector of $H_{2}$ only if $\varphi=0$; the total
momentum operators $P_{R,j}$ are self-adjoint with no nonzero eigenvectors in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$, so the model possesses no normalisable
state of definite total momentum, and by the stationary-state criterion no
product of a centre-of-mass state with a relative bound state is a stationary
state of the two-body system;

(e) *Reading.* The reduced mass obeys $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$ and
satisfies $\mu\le\min\{m_{1},m_{2}\}$ with $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$
at fixed $m_{1}$; the model reads the one-centre model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
$m_{1}$ as the fixed-nucleus limiting description, and the relative energies
$\mathcal E_{n}$ are strictly weaker in magnitude than the fixed-nucleus
energies $-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
two-body model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured mass, charge
or level, no transition, photon or radiation statement, no binding or
formation dynamics, and no identification of the model with a laboratory
atom beyond the tested identification of clause (e) of the model definition.
